rulings.note: Rousing Sergeant literally galvanizes troops into the ETB vigilance buff; Vanguard options are more self-descriptive than team-buff-descriptive, and 'Vanguard' recurs as bait across this batch's option pools so keeping it out avoids downstream collisions.

Grafting Elder nails the counter-via-targeted-spells mechanic ('graft' = attaching), though 'Elder' echoes pool's existing Elder of the Grove/Apex Elder mildly; still clear best fit over the Beast/generic-Shaman options.
Momentary Exile is the most literal description of a one-beat exile-then-return; Vanishing Act is a decent runner-up but reads slightly punnier/lighter than the pool's register.

Skyline Tactician avoids two traps: the Angel-Soldier option silently implies flying not present in the spec, and 'Wing Commander' echoes pool's existing Knight Commander pattern; Tactician keeps it clean.
Pinning Lancer vividly matches 'taps a blocker on attack' (pin = immobilize), reads as natural Magic cadence; Shackling overstates the effect and Wayclearer is a slightly awkward compound.
Flashborn Sprite is a direct, elegant pun on the card's own Flash keyword feeding its own growth; Ambush/Ambuscade options collide with pool's existing Ambush Djinn.

Riposte Pyromancer captures reactive instant-speed casting plus the red half of UR without repeating 'Flash-' already spent on WU_1-2's pick; Warden of Hidden Hours reads too purple/abstract for the mechanic.
Borrowed Wings is an elegant, precise pun for temporary flight-granting; Windward Blessing's 'Blessing' reads white, not a fit for this mono-U card.
Undertow Recall leans into blue's water/knowledge idiom and 'Recall' double-covers both bounce and draw; the Strategic/Tactical options read more militaristic than bluish and miss the draw half.
Covenant Scholar is self-consistent (the creature is literally both chosen tribes) and boosts scarce Merfolk (pool count 2); Twin Circle Sage is clever but 'Sage' is already a 3x-used pool suffix.
Eager Familiar ties perfectly to a wizard's-companion-grows-with-knowledge flavor, introduces a brand-new subtype, and dodges the Human/Wizard oversaturation the Apprentice option carries.
Spellrider is the tightest single-word pun for 'gains flying when you cast noncreature spells'; Arcane Drifter is offered twice (dead duplicate slot) and reads generically vague by comparison.
Tidewatcher nails the reactive/opponent's-turn timing with a clean blue idiom and boosts scarce Merfolk; Interloping Scholar has the cleverer pun but doubles down on oversaturated Human+Wizard.
Warding Shell covers both halves of the effect (shell=toughness, ward=hexproof) with sea-shell imagery appropriate to blue; Chrysalis Ward's imagery reads more green than blue.
Rootbinder Druid is clean of collisions; Landwaker is the more literal 'turns land into creature' pun but echoes pool's existing Awakener closely enough to flag.

Earthwatch Guardian is the only option that specifically nods to the land-vigilance-granting clause; all four collide somewhat with pool's crowded Guard/Guardian/Sentry/Sentinel vocabulary, but this one has the strongest mechanic payoff to justify it.
Proud Broodmother turns the +1/+1-per-creature-ETB trigger into a literal 'pride' pun; Bramble Acolyte doesn't engage the mechanic and collides with pool's Wicked Acolyte.
Deathbloom Tender is a lovely death-to-growth pun matching the dies-trigger-counter mechanic, and lands on Elf Druid rather than piling onto the Human count like the other three.
Goblin Cannoneer vividly frames the sacrificed creature as ammunition fired at any target; Bloodstoke Goblin collides with the pool's already-saturated Blood- prefix (7 existing entries).
Thornspark Shaman balances both colors and precisely puns 'spark' onto the bonus-damage clause while avoiding Human tax; Bramblefang Provoker doesn't engage the spell-damage mechanic at all.
Warhorn Rampager cleanly signals 'gets fired up when the pack charges'; Packfire Hound is the more evocative pun but stacks onto a pool already carrying two Hound-named cards.
Landgrown Sapling is a precise literal-growth pun (a sapling growing from each new plot of land) and lands on the less-saturated Elemental type.
Scorchgrown Giant precisely puns 'grown by scorching sorceries'; Wildfire Colossus directly collides with the pool's existing Wildfire Devil.
Sunder the Gears matches the pool's established 'Verb the Noun' convention (Awaken the Stone/Vault) with vivid mechanical imagery; Shattering Strike collides with pool's existing Final/Twin Strike.
Spark Instigator cleanly puns 'activating an ability provokes damage' without the mild anachronism risk of Flintlock (a gunpowder-era word) or that option's collision with pool's Goblin Duelist.

Wildwood Scout gives up a hair of literal precision (Homestead Pioneer more exactly matches 'land enters battlefield') to land on the far less-saturated Elf/Scout combo instead of Human; Scout is also a brand-new subtype.
Vigil Chanter ties the casting trigger ('chanter' = one who casts) to the granted keyword itself; Glade Marshal is off-color (glade reads green) and collides with pool's two existing Marshal cards.
Renewed Vigil is a clean double-pun (renewed=untap, vigil=vigilance) offered twice in the package (dead duplicate slot); Second Wind/Slack Tide only cover the untap half.

Chapter Recruiter directly matches the 'creature enters, gain counter' trigger via 'recruiter'; Muster Sergeant is mechanically the strongest pun but collides with this batch's own Rousing Sergeant pick, and Warband Elder collides with Grafting Elder.
Battlecry Adjutant is a tight double-military-pun for a static team anthem; Frenzied Instigator was ruled out for colliding with this batch's own Spark Instigator pick.

Zephyr Caller is self-consistent (a wind-djinn that calls flight onto allies when it casts) and avoids piling onto pool's already-saturated Angel count (4 existing); Skyward Tactician was ruled out for colliding with this batch's own Skyline Tactician pick.

Triage Cleric is a vivid, precise battlefield-medic pun for 'gain life when a damage-ETB creature enters,' offered twice in the package (dead duplicate slot); Convalescent Firebrand reads as an internally contradictory combination.

batchNotes:
Subtype spread across the 26 creature picks is healthy and deliberately census-aware: Human appears 8 times (Rousing Sergeant, Skyline Tactician, Pinning Lancer, Riposte Pyromancer, Vigil Chanter, Chapter Recruiter, Battlecry Adjutant, Triage Cleric) versus 62 in the existing pool — kept to under a third of this batch despite several packages offering nothing but Human options (RW_0-1's "populous tribe" design literally requires Human, so that one is non-discretionary). Diversity wins: two Merfolk (Covenant Scholar, Tidewatcher, boosting a tribe sitting at only 2 in the pool), a brand-new Familiar subtype (Eager Familiar) and a brand-new Scout subtype (Wildwood Scout), plus Djinn, Illusion, Elemental, Giant, Faerie, and three Elf/Druid picks spread across different cards rather than clustering. Deliberately avoided the Angel option for WU_1-0 (Wing Commander/Angel Soldier) since it would have silently granted flying not present in that card's spec — the clearest implied-keyword trap in the batch — and avoided a second Angel for RW_2-1 to not pile onto the pool's already-substantial 4 existing Angels.

Two intentional but flagged word-repeats survive: "Vigil" appears in both Vigil Chanter (GW_2-2) and Renewed Vigil (GU_3-0) — both cards mechanically grant vigilance, so the shared root is earned rather than lazy, but it's still the same word twice in one 32-card set. Similarly "spark" surfaces in both Thornspark Shaman (RG_1-0) and Spark Instigator (RW_3-2), both red damage-payoff creatures — again mechanically motivated but worth a second look if a harder anti-repetition pass is wanted. Everywhere else a same-word collision was live (Vanguard bait in GW_0-2/RW_1-1, Sergeant in GW_0-2/RW_0-1, Elder in GW_3-1/RW_0-1, Instigator in RW_3-2/RW_1-1, Tactician in WU_1-0/RW_2-1) I deliberately picked away from the second occurrence, which is why several individual rulings look like they left points on the table relative to a raw per-card score — those are batch-hygiene tradeoffs, not oversights. Register held close to the pool's plain-classic-Magic idiom throughout; the one deliberate register override was ruling out "Flintlock Duelist" for RW_3-2 on anachronism grounds (gunpowder-trigger imagery in an otherwise non-firearms pool).
